prompt_en: A natural photographic scene of a woman using wearable mechanical assistance in a small fabrication workshop, with readable mechanical connections and visible body-side ownership and contact. Use the supplied reference for her visible facial appearance and dark bob haircut. She has paused at a bench clamp, holding its lever with her left palm; her steady attention and relaxed mouth give the working moment a quiet personal presence. Her anatomical left arm is the near arm on image-right. One external support frame lies outside that human arm and over her plain charcoal work shirt. An open shoulder harness presents its exposed root at the front outer edge of her left shoulder. A rigid exposed bracket runs continuously from that harness root to a clearly bounded upper-arm cuff, with both fixed joints facing the camera. An external elbow hinge visibly links that upper-arm cuff to a forearm cuff along the same outer side. Her bare human wrist continues beyond the forearm cuff into her left hand, visibly distinct from the end of the frame. Her left elbow is mildly bent and held clear of her ribs; air gaps separate the frame from the torso, and the whole external route faces the camera. The left palm lies across the broad lever handle; the palm edge touching its top surface, thumb beside the handle and handle entering the clamp are visible together. Her other hand hangs freely on image-left. The camera sees her from slightly in front of her left side, framed from head to mid-thigh with space around the entire shoulder-to-handle route. Broad window light models her face and gives each mechanical connection an edged highlight against a subdued workshop background. The face, linked arm support and hand contact carry the photograph together, with natural skin texture and restrained metallic reflections.
